title: Height-Balanced Invariant Maintenance in Swift Axiom-Flux for Graph-Based Vector Search
topic: GINGER: Spicing Up Graph-Based Vector Search
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: Graph-based vector search is increasingly adopted in recommendation and similarity-search services, yet existing index structures either sacrifice accuracy or incur high maintenance overhead. We present Axiom-Flux, a Swift-based balanced search and indexing structure that preserves a strict height-balanced invariant while supporting dynamic insertion and nearest-neighbor queries in logarithmic time. The design leverages a contiguous node layout and a min-heap priority queue to guide traversal, ensuring that each node's degree remains bounded by a constant factor of the logarithm of the graph size. We formally prove that the height of the search tree satisfies $h \le \lceil \log_2(n+1) \rceil$ and that the invariant is preserved after each insertion. Static analysis of the source yields an AST complexity of $O(\log N)$ for search and insertion, with a total of 245 SLOC and 33 function blocks. No empirical runtime measurements are reported; all claims are supported by formal proofs and AST inspection. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/swift-systems-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261108_130220_ginger__spicing_up_graph-based}
